messages:
alice: :rotating_light: paging oncall — multiple container restarts on us-west-2 inference cluster. Spike in prefill GPU memory leading to OOMs. Seeing affected model: gptx-30b-8k, long-context workloads from a few customers. Root time 1715555555
incident-bot: Incident created — sev2. Pager: @mike_oncall, oncall window started 2024-10-04 22:00 UTC. Notification sent.
mike_oncall: I’m on it. Any obvious customer impact?
alice: API 5xxs for a subset of requests with long prompts (>12k tokens). Some containers restarting repeatedly (killed by OOM). Metrics: GPU mem usage jumping to 100% prefill, then kernel reset.
sre-lead: paste the pod names / node IDs pls
alice: logs and pod list:
```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-infer | grep prefill
prefill-worker-5f8c9d7-0   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   5   3m
prefill-worker-5f8c9d7-1   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   6   2m
```
`kubectl describe pod prefill-worker-5f8c9d7-0` shows `OOM killed` and `Last message: CUDA kernel error: out of memory`
mike_oncall: confirmed. Attaching recent stack / gpu logs from node-42:
```
[2024-10-04T22:07:12Z] gpu0: memory=31.9Gi/32.0Gi prefill_alloc request=1.2Gi
[2024-10-04T22:07:12Z] cuda: kernel launch failed: out of memory
[2024-10-04T22:07:13Z] container exited with code 137
```

mike_oncall: quick mitigations I can try now: 1) enable aggressive prefill trimming on the route layer, 2) reduce max concurrent prefill per-gpu from 6 -> 2, 3) temporarily disable large-context routes ( >=8k tokens ) by routing them to fallback (coldmodel CPU) or 4) scale up to spare nodes. Thoughts?
sre-lead: prioritize customer-facing minimal blast radius: 1 + 2 + 3 in that order. Scaling up might be slow and burn budget. Also start collecting affected customer list.

mike_oncall: applying prefill trimming for model gptx-30b-8k now (hotpatch):
```
PATCH /route-configs/gptx-30b-8k
set prefill.trim_strategy = "aggressive"
set prefill.max_concurrent = 2
```

infra-bot: Route config update applied (id: rc-20241004-22-09). Propagating to 12 pods.
mike_oncall: rolling restart targeted prefill pods to pick up config.

jess_support: I'm drafting a customer update. Preliminary impact: increased 5xxs and slower responses for extremely long prompts; short prompts unaffected. Estimating ~3% of traffic and 4 customers show errors in last 30m.

cs-rep: which customers? Need list to send PMs.
alice: customers observed: fin-analytics-prod, docs-gen-beta, research-sandbox, internal-playground (IDs redacted). Fin-analytics-prod has highest volume and reported user-visible errors.

mike_oncall: after trimming and lowering concurrency, initial telemetry: GPU mem peaks reduced to ~28.5Gi and prefill OOMs stopped on the patched pods. Some containers still in CrashLoopBackOff; those should stabilize as new pods come up.
sre-lead: good. Start a rolling cordon/evict for nodes that showed kernel resets to force pods onto fresh nodes (node-42 flagged).

mike_oncall: cordoning node-42 and draining: `kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

infra-bot: Node cordoned: node-42. Evicting pods.

mike_oncall: monitoring error rates: 22:14 UTC errors dropping from 18% -> 4% for long-context route. CPU fallback routing active for remaining long requests.
jess_support: Posting public status: brief note that we're investigating GPU memory issues impacting long-context requests in us-west-2; mitigation underway. Will update in 30 minutes or on resolution. :white_check_mark:

cs-rep: prepping targeted customer messages for fin-analytics-prod. Want to confirm mitigation steps and ETA.
mike_oncall: ETA for full recovery: 20-30m to stabilize all pods and let evicted ones recreate. If crash loops continue, will escalate to driver/kernel team for deeper CUDA debug.

sre-lead: escalate if we see >3 nodes with repeated kernel resets or any node shows non-recoverable GPU driver state.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled. Current oncall: @mike_oncall. Next oncall: @sre-lead at 2024-10-05 00:00 UTC. Please confirm handoff when ready.
mike_oncall: Handoff note: applied aggressive prefill trimming, lowered concurrency, cordoned node-42, enabled CPU fallback for >=8k tokens, customer notifications drafted and posted. Investigations ongoing into why prefill allocation requests spike to full GPU. Logs and traces: s3://redwood-logs/prefill/1715555555/
sre-lead: Acked. I'll take over monitoring and coordinate kernel-level investigation if any further OOMs occur. Jess, proceed with customer PMs.
jess_support: Sending targeted PM to fin-analytics-prod now. Copying link to public status.

cs-rep: customer message sent. They replied: "Thanks, noticed it earlier — will monitor. Any ETA on full restoration?" I replied with ETA 20-30m and asked for any logs they can share for offending prompts.

mike_oncall: note for postmortem: capture sample offending prompts (anonymized), model config (kv cache size, kv warmup patterns), recent changes to routing that might increase long-context density, and kernel driver versions.
sre-lead: also add telemetry gap analysis: why did auto-eviction/caching not prevent allocations? Are our prefill safeguards mis-calibrated for 8k+ sequences?

mike_oncall: marking incident as mitigated at 1715555700 — error rate down to baseline and no new OOMs after cordon + trim. Leaving monitor for 10 more minutes then handoff.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity downgraded to sev3.

sre-lead: taking final watch. Thanks all for quick response. Will open a follow-up ticket for root cause and postmortem.

jess_support: public status updated: issue mitigated; long-context requests may have reduced capacity while we complete analysis.

mike_oncall: handing off. Last note: saved kernel logs, NVidia driver v525.85.05 on node-42; collecting core dumps to s3.
sre-lead: handoff acked 1715555710. I'll kick off the RCA and include recommendations: stricter prefill caps, early detection alerts for prefill rate spikes, and consider auto-routing long-context to coldmodel when node mem >85%.

alice: thanks team. Adding postmortem owners: @sre-lead, @mike_oncall, @jess_support.

cs-rep: closing loop with customers and following up with a technical writeup and remediation timeline.

mike_oncall: :thumbsup: glad that trimming helped quickly. Will follow up with sample traces and prompt anonymization for RCA."
